title: Master Honen's Dharma Words on Attaining Peace of Mind through the Recitation of the Buddha's Name
author: Zhanran
excerpt: Q: A work circulating online, the Forty-Eight Sayings of Master Honen (also called the Dharma Words on Peace of Mind in Buddha-Recitation), was carefully selected from the Complete Works of Master Honen by the Dharma Master Huijing (whose background is discussed in What Is the Primal Vow Dharma Gate), and is claimed to be "word on the recitation of the Buddha's name that brings peace of mind." Can it really bring peace of mind?

inline.s: Those who recite the Buddha's name must first of all make one thing clear:
What is the condition for rebirth in the Pure Land?
Otherwise one will be heading in exactly the wrong direction,
and ruin the great matter of his own rebirth.
Q: A work circulating online, the
Forty-Eight
Sayings of Master Honen (also called the Dharma Words on Peace of Mind in Buddha-Recitation), was carefully selected by the Dharma Master Huijing (whose background is discussed in
What Is the Primal Vow Dharma Gate
) from the Complete Works of Master Honen, and is claimed to be "word on the recitation of the Buddha's name that brings peace of mind." Can it really bring peace of mind?
A: At the very start this collection of Dharma Words relates: Master Honen

“based on the Pure Land thought of Master Shandao, the manifestation of Amitābha, and founded the Japanese Pure Land school. Master Honen obtained the very marrow of Master Shandao, and entered the Pure Land school through Master Shandao's passage on the karma of right samādhi.”
In fact, this collection of Dharma Words entirely contradicts the scriptures and treatises, and entirely contradicts Master Shandao's own teaching.

This collection of Dharma Words comprises forty-eight articles. To save space I will take only the first article as an example to lay bare the essence of its error and falsity; the discerning will naturally draw the rest from one instance.
The Dharma Words say:
1. The karma of right samādhi is the recitation of the Buddha's name; whoever recites the name is certain to be reborn, because of the Buddha's primal vow.”
Those who recite the Buddha's name must first of all make one thing clear:
What is the condition for rebirth in the Pure Land?
Otherwise one will be heading in exactly the wrong direction, and ruin the great matter of his own rebirth.
The condition for rebirth is:
ten consecutive recitations at the moment of death.

This condition for rebirth was taught by Master Shandao, the manifestation of Amitābha, by Master Yongming, the manifestation of Amitābha, and by the sages Master Tanluan and Master Daochuo, who attained realization in their practice;
it is the measure of the words of the sages
(See in detail the article
The Condition for Rebirth: Ten Consecutive Recitations at Death

.) Yet Master Honen absurdly claims that "whoever recites the name is certain to be reborn." This is wholly deceptive talk! To believe and feel at ease with such deceiving nonsense is nothing less than shutting one's eyes and fooling oneself. When the great matter of rebirth is ruined, regret will be too late!
[The measure of the words of the sages] This is what the sages have spoken, correct and without error, and certain to be believed and accepted.
As for
“the karma of right samādhi”
, Master Shandao's own words in the Four-Fascicle Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra are:
Single-mindedly
recite the name of Amitābha; whether walking, standing, sitting or lying, without regard to the length of time,
thought after thought without forsaking
(each thought not being dragged away by deluded thoughts)
— this is called
the karma of right samādhi
, because it accords with the vow of that Buddha
(Amitābha)

(Translation: Single-mindedly reciting the name of Amitābha Buddha, whether walking, standing, sitting or lying, without regard to the length of time, and thought after thought without forsaking — this is called the karma of right samādhi, and this is because it accords with the vow of Amitābha Buddha.)

[Single-minded] Master Tanluan, in his Commentary on the Treatise on Rebirth, taught: Single-mindedness means thought succeeding thought in an unbroken stream, with no other thought intruding. (See in detail
Master Tanluan's Pure Land Teaching

) [Thought after thought without forsaking] Every single thought is the name of Amitābha. [Right samādhi] Correct concentration. When the body and mind are pure and clear, without scattered distraction, it is called right samādhi. [Karma] The activity of body, speech and mind. [Because it accords with that Buddha's vow] “Single-mindedly reciting the name of Amitābha, whether walking, standing, sitting or lying, without regard to the length of time, thought after thought without forsaking” — this is because it accords with the vow of Amitābha Buddha.
Master Shandao is the manifestation of Amitābha; his words are the words of Amitābha Buddha. From this we may know that when sentient beings
recite the Buddha's name single-mindedly, thought after thought without forsaking
, this accords with the vow of that Buddha (Amitābha). Therefore
to recite the Buddha's name with a scattered mind is to go against the Buddha's vow!
[Recitation with a scattered mind] Uttering the Buddha's name with the mouth while the mind dwells on other things.
Concerning recitation with a scattered mind
Master Hanshan, in his Song on Wasted Effort, taught:
You may mouth the name of Amitābha with a mind all scattered; though you cry until your throat bursts, it is all in vain.”
[Wasted Effort] “

Waste,” to spend time and energy; “Effort,” useless, labor lost. “Wasted Effort” means spending time and energy with no actual result, which is what is commonly called doing useless work. In the Song on Wasted Effort, Master Hanshan points out the common mistaken paths on which practice is wasted in vain, and how to step out of them.
(See in detail
A Commentary on the Song on Wasted Effort
I now transcribe and annotate Master Hanshan's teaching as follows:

[Reciting the Buddha's name is easy, but faith is hard; when the heart and mouth are not one, it is all wasted effort. You may mouth the name of Amitābha with a mind all scattered; though you cry until your throat bursts, it is all in vain.]

Reciting the Buddha's name is easy, but a mind of true faith is hard; when heart and mouth are not one (the heart not truly believing: the mouth reciting the Buddha's name while the mind dwells on other things), it is always wasted effort (altogether labor lost); if with the mouth one recites Amitābha Buddha while the mind dwells on other things, though the throat is cried hoarse it is all in vain.

[Faith] A mind of true faith; when the heart and the mouth are not one, that is falsehood. Hence the next line: “when the heart and mouth are not one, it is always wasted effort.” [True faith] The meaning of being honest, of not deceiving.
Master Shandao is saying:
single-minded
recitation of the Buddha's name is the karma of right samādhi;
single-minded
recitation of the Buddha's name is relying on the primal vow of that Buddha (Amitābha).
But Master Honen, with a hidden motive, took this teaching and
cut off the most crucial
“single-minded”
two characters
, and
falsely altered it to:
The karma of right samādhi is the recitation of the Buddha's name; whoever recites the name is certain to be reborn, because of the Buddha's primal vow.”
Single-minded

— this is the key to the correct practice of the Pure Land school. Master Shandao, the manifestation of Amitābha, taught: in reciting the sutras, in contemplation, in recollection, in venerating the Buddha, in reciting the Buddha's name, and in praise and offerings, one must be
single-minded
for it to be right practice.
Master Shandao says:

“Now there are two kinds of practice: first, right practice; second, mixed practice. As for right practice: to rely wholly on the sutras on rebirth and practice them — this is called right practice. What is it?
single-mindedly
recite the Contemplation Sutra, the Amitābha Sutra, the Infinite Life Sutra and so forth;
single-mindedly
apply the mind to reflecting on, contemplating, and recollecting the adornments of the twofold recompense of that land. If one venerates, then
single-mindedly
venerate that Buddha; if one utters the name, then
single-mindedly
utter that Buddha's name; if one praises and makes offerings, then
single-mindedly
praise and make offerings to that Buddha.
This is called right
(Four-Fascicle Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra)
Therefore, Master Shandao is saying
single-minded
recitation of the Buddha's name is the karma of right samādhi
; yet Master Honen falsified it into: recitation of the Buddha's name is the karma of right samādhi. He cut off the most crucial
“single-minded”
two characters. When the mind dwells on a single object, that is called calmness. I ask: without single-mindedness, how could it be
right samādhi
? If there is no right samādhi to begin with, whence the
karma of right samādhi
Moreover, the correct content of the “karma of right samādhi” has been falsified by Master Honen, and yet Huijing and his fellows still say that “Master Honen
obtained
(?) the very marrow of Master Shandao, and
entered
(?) the Pure Land school through Master Shandao's passage on the karma of right samādhi” — this is altogether deceiving nonsense! Read this Dharma Words alongside
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teaching
and you will clearly see how Master Honen falsified Master Shandao's teaching to establish the Primal Vow Dharma Gate
. Yet Huijing and his fellows still loudly proclaim that Master Honen “
based
(?) his teaching on Master Shandao, the manifestation of Amitābha, and founded the Japanese Pure Land school.”
Master Shandao's
marrow
is:
single-mindedly upholding the Name, thought after thought without forsaking.
Because this is the karma of right samādhi, and accords with the vow of Amitābha Buddha. Master Shandao taught:
Single-mindedly
recite the name of Amitābha; whether walking, standing, sitting or lying, without regard to the length of time,
thought after thought without forsaking
(each thought not being dragged away by deluded thoughts)
— this is called
the karma of right samādhi
, because it accords with the vow of that Buddha
(Amitābha)
(Four-Fascicle Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra)
It is precisely because upholding the Name is easy
(precisely because upholding the Name and reciting it is easier to accomplish than contemplation of the Buddha)
that in continuity one is reborn
. If one can be thought after thought continuous, even until the end of life
(the one who thus practices to the end of life)
, then of ten, ten are reborn; of a hundred, a hundred are reborn.
I pray all people reflect well, and that whether walking, standing, sitting or lying, they must
arouse the mind and restrain the self
, day and night never ceasing
(day and night never ceasing from thought after thought 's continuity)

, so that with the final thought's death, the next thought is born [in the Pure Land]. Forever enjoying the unconditioned Dharma-bliss, and even attaining Buddhahood — how could this not be a delight!”
(The Treatise on the Two Kinds of Practice, Exclusive and Mixed; for the annotation see in detail
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teaching
[In continuity one is reborn]
At the moment of death, when the thought of recitation is continuous
(not broken by deluded thoughts)
, one is reborn in the Western Paradise of Ultimate Bliss.
The “continuity” spoken of here is the one spoken of in the Chapter on Perfect Penetration by the Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta through the Recitation of the Buddha's Name, namely
“pure thought succeeding pure thought”

, that is, thought after thought of recitation continuously succeeding, with no deluded thought mingled amid (if a deluded thought is mingled in, it is not continuity). “Thought after thought for the duration of life” is precisely to make thought after thought continuous so that it becomes a settled habit and nature, in order to guarantee the ten consecutive recitations at death.
Ten consecutive recitations at death — this is the condition for rebirth.
(See in detail the article
The Condition for Rebirth: Ten Consecutive Recitations at Death

[Arouse the mind and restrain the self] Arousing the mind means inciting the mind to do what ought to be done; restraining the self means holding the self back from doing what ought not to be done. These four words, “arouse the mind and restrain the self,” are a mighty weapon for overcoming difficulty and sweeping away hindrances.
[Day and night never ceasing] Day and night never ceasing from the continuity of thought after thought.

[With the death of the final thought, the next thought is born] This says: because the thought of recitation is continuous, therefore the very last thought at death must be the thought of recitation, and
after that last thought one is
at once reborn in the Western Paradise of Ultimate Bliss.
Single-mindedly upholding the Name is supremely excellent.
For single-mindedly upholding the Name, the three studies — precepts, concentration and wisdom — are all complete:

Precepts are for guarding against faults; if one can single-mindedly uphold the Name, then no evil can enter — this is precepts. Concentration is for removing scatteredness; if one single-mindedly holds the name, the mind does not grasp at anything else — this is concentration. Wisdom is clear discernment: if one contemplates the Buddha-name so that every character is clear and distinct, and also perceives that the one who recites and what is recited are both unobtainable — this is wisdom. Therefore single-mindedly upholding the Name is precepts, concentration and wisdom.

[The three studies] The study of precepts, the study of concentration, and the study of wisdom. Precepts are the prohibitions, set forth in the treasury of the vinaya, which keep people from committing all the evil deeds of body, speech and mind; concentration is meditative calm, set forth in the treasury of the sutras, which enables people to still and clarify the mind; wisdom is insight, set forth in the treasury of the commentaries, which enables people to discover the truth and cut off ignorance. By cultivating these three studies, one may through precepts attain concentration, and through concentration produce wisdom, and ultimately obtain the taint-free fruit of the path; therefore the three studies are also called the three taint-free studies.
For single-mindedly upholding the Name, the six perfections and the myriad practices are all fulfilled:

Single-mindedly upholding the Name, all conditions are naturally cast aside — this is the perfection of giving; single-mindedly upholding the Name, all evil naturally ceases — this is the perfection of precepts; single-mindedly upholding the Name, the mind naturally becomes gentle — this is the perfection of patience; single-mindedly upholding the Name, one never falls back — this is the perfection of diligence; single-mindedly upholding the Name, no other thought arises — this is the perfection of meditation; single-mindedly upholding the Name, right mindfulness is clear and distinct — this is the perfection of wisdom. Extending this to all practices, single-mindedly upholding the Name fulfills the myriad practices.

[The six perfections] The six methods of ferrying across from this shore of the suffering of birth and death to the shore of nirvanic bliss, namely giving, precepts, patience, diligence, meditation, and wisdom. Giving can ferry one over miserliness; precepts can ferry one over transgression; patience can ferry one over anger; diligence can ferry one over sloth; meditation can ferry one over distraction; wisdom can ferry one over ignorance. [The six perfections and the myriad practices] The Bodhicitta Treatise says:
“Again, through the three asankhya kalpas
(three great asankhya kalpas)
, the six perfections and the myriad practices are all fulfilled, and then one realizes the Buddha-fruit.”
Therefore Master Shandao, the manifestation of Amitābha, taught:
single-minded
upholding of the Name is the karma of right samādhi.
Because
only when the three studies of precepts, concentration and wisdom are all complete, and the six perfections and the myriad practices are all fulfilled, is it the karma of right samādhi.
Master Shandao is saying
single-minded
recitation of the Buddha's name is the karma of right samādhi; yet Master Honen falsified it into: recitation of the Buddha's name is the karma of right samādhi, cutting off the most crucial
“single-minded”
two characters. When the mind dwells on a single object, that is called calmness. I ask: without single-mindedness, how could it be
right samādhi
? Reciting the Buddha's name with a scattered mind, delusions unceasing, whence the
right samādhi

? If there is no right samādhi, whence the karma of right samādhi? It is common to see Huijing, Jingzong and others, who loudly trumpet recitation with a scattered mind and “reciting the name ensures rebirth,” going about preaching that what they practice is the karma of right samādhi — truly shameless!
Moreover, Master Shandao states it clearly and distinctly:
single-minded
upholding of the Name, thought after thought without forsaking — only this accords with the vow of that Buddha (Amitābha).
But Master Honen cut off the most crucial
“single-minded”

two characters, falsifying it into: recitation of the Buddha's name is relying on the Buddha's primal vow, and so drew the absurd conclusion “whoever recites the name is certain to be reborn,” loudly trumpeting “reciting the name ensures rebirth”! I now copy out a few passages from the Dharma Words on Peace of Mind in Buddha-Recitation, and the whole picture may be glimpsed:
Amitābha urges that the one who recites the Buddha's name is certain to come to be welcomed; Śākyamuni urges that the one who recites the Buddha's name is certain to attain rebirth.”
Even though one has doubt, if he recites the Buddha's name he gains rebirth. Reciting the Buddha's name amid doubt, he gains rebirth.”
It is no hindrance not to understand its meaning or not to understand its wording; merely by relying on reciting the name, one is certain to attain rebirth.”
Reciting the Buddha's name has no deep meaning; the one who recites only knows that ‘reciting the Buddha's name brings certain rebirth.’”
Apart from thinking only that the primal vow is not empty and that reciting the name brings certain rebirth, the mind has nothing to which it clings.”
The one who only knows that reciting the name brings certain rebirth, and who recites the Buddha's name with all his heart, gains rebirth.”
He who but knows that sentient beings who recite the name are certain to attain rebirth
then naturally possesses the three minds
(the sincere mind, the deep mind, and the mind that transfers merit and resolves)
[In the Contemplation Sutra (the Sutra of Contemplation on Amitayus, for short the Contemplation Sutra), the Buddha says:

“As for the highest grade of the highest birth: if any sentient being aspires to be reborn in that land, he arouses the three minds and is at once reborn. What are the three? First, the sincere mind; second, the deep mind; third, the mind that transfers merit and resolves toward rebirth. One who possesses the three minds is certain to be reborn in that land.”

This says that whoever arouses the three minds is certain to be reborn in the Western Paradise of Ultimate Bliss, and at the highest grade of the highest birth. Yet Master Honen inverted it into: “sentient beings who recite the name
will certainly
attain rebirth, then
naturally possess
the three minds”!]
The
essential secret
of the Pure Land school lies in this: no matter who it is, whosoever recites the Buddha's name is reborn. Though there be an evil person without peer in the world
(none with whom to compare)
, if he recites Namo Amitābha Buddha, even with a single thought he gains rebirth.”
[Look! This is the
essential secret
of the Primal Vow Dharma Gate: the worst evil person in the world
(the evil person without peer)

, so long as he has recited a single line of the Buddha's name, gains rebirth. With this Dharma Words on Peace of Mind, the one who stops at nothing evil has a guarantee and loses all fear! In the Amitābha Sutra spoken by the Buddha, the Buddha says:
“It is not by little good roots, merit, blessing, causes and conditions that one attains birth in that land.”

Yet Master Honen openly proclaims: so long as one recites a single line of the Buddha's name, he may do any evil whatsoever, and at death he will be reborn in the Western Paradise of Ultimate Bliss, forever enjoying all bliss. Is this the Dharma? They also loudly trumpet “the evil person is the true capacity,” and defameously declare this to be “the primal vow of Amitābha.”
For example, the Dharma Master Huijing, in his Essential Meaning of Master Shandao, says:
“One must know that the aim of the Contemplation Sutra is to make manifest
the primal vow of Amitābha
the evil person is the true capacity
The Dharma Master Xinyuan, a disciple who took refuge with the Dharma Master Huijing, says in Amitābha's Deliverance Is the Evil Person as True Capacity:
“Let us now look at what kind of sentient being Amitābha's deliverance takes as its true capacity — the evil person as true capacity.”
Master Honen, in the Dharma Words on Peace of Mind in Buddha-Recitation, says:
“If one commits the five heinous acts, and comes to hear the six-character name
(comes to hear “Namo Amitābha Buddha”)
, the fiery cart departs of itself
(the fiery cart of hell departs of itself)
, and the lotus dais comes at once to welcome.”

This is nothing less than inciting evil deeds! Such incitement not only causes the person concerned, at the end of life, not only to fail to attain rebirth but to fall into the evil destinies to receive retribution; it is moreover gravely disruptive to society, damaging to the reputation of Buddhism, and harmful to others.

[The five heinous acts] The five heinous offenses: the five kinds of sin that are supremely contrary to reason, namely killing one's father, killing one's mother, killing an arhat, causing the Buddha's body to bleed, and disrupting the harmony of the sangha. These five are acts of extreme evil; if one commits any of them, he falls into the Avici hell, and for this reason they are also called the inexpiable karma.
As for the karmic teaching that “good deeds meet with good recompense and evil deeds with evil recompense,”
in the Preface to the Verification of Karmic Retribution Master Yinguang taught: karmic retribution is the
mighty authority
by which the sages of the world and the sages beyond the world govern the state, secure society, and ferry sentient beings to deliverance.
The Buddhist scriptures expound the karmic retribution of the three times most thoroughly. To speak of it in brief, it is this:
“Would you know the cause of your former life? What you receive in this life is it. Would you know the fruit of your future life? What you do in this life is it.”
(The original text:

“Karmic retribution is the mighty authority by which the sages of the world and beyond the world govern the state and ferry sentient beings to deliverance. ... The Buddhist scriptures speak of the karmic retribution of the three times most thoroughly. To speak of it in brief, it is said: Would you know the cause of your former life? What you receive in this life is it. Would you know the fruit of your future life? What you do in this life is it.”

Therefore the karmic teaching of good and evil retribution is of the utmost importance! It leads people to cease from evil and practice good, so as to leave the evil retribution and attain the good recompense, and thereby govern the state, secure society, and ferry sentient beings to deliverance.
Therefore Master Yinguang strongly promoted the teaching of karmic retribution, and taught:
“Karmic retribution is the mighty authority by which the sages of the world and beyond the world govern the state and ferry sentient beings to deliverance.
(Because)

if karmic retribution is not promoted, then the good cannot be encouraged and the evil cannot be punished; only the greatest worthies can abide by their lot and follow the Way, while all the rest, who would not prefer to give their minds free rein and take pleasure for a single lifetime?” “
When everyone understands karmic retribution, that is the way of great order; when everyone does not understand karmic retribution, that is the way of great disorder.
(The Collected Essays of Master Yinguang
Preface to the Summary of the Notes of Master Ji Wen-da)
“Moral virtue and benevolence are the virtue of our nature, originally inherent in us;
karmic retribution is truly the mighty authority of heaven and earth's transforming nurture

.” “If one understands karmic retribution, then good and evil, fortune and misfortune are clear as though seen in fire; whoever would not choose to seek the auspicious and avoid the inauspicious, to escape disaster and gain blessing?”
(The Collected Essays of Master Yinguang
Discourse on Reversing the Calamities, Protecting the Country and Saving the People, and Restoring the Source)

And the Primal Vow Dharma Gate trumpets “the evil person is the true capacity” — this inverts the karmic law that “good deeds meet with good recompense, evil deeds with evil recompense,” to delude and confuse sentient beings. It incites people to think: evil has no evil retribution, but rather a great blessing; you need only recite a single line of the Buddha's name, and you may freely do every evil deed, and after death go straight to the Western Paradise of Ultimate Bliss to enjoy all bliss forever, because
the evil person
is
the true capacity

of Amitābha's deliverance. (During the war of aggression against China, the chaplains sent out with the army by the Japanese Primal Vow Dharma Gate incited the Japanese soldiers precisely in this way; see in detail
The Practice of Master Honen's Teaching
Evil
(including the five heinous offenses)
has no evil retribution; on the contrary it has great blessing — a single line of the Buddha's name has become the amulet that protects one from the consequences of evil deeds!
This

entirely contradicts the Buddhist scriptures, violates the karmic law of good and evil retribution, destroys the karmic education of good and evil retribution, and incites the hearts of people toward evil.

Such nonsense — do you feel at ease after reading it? As disciples of the Buddha, we should not only not propagate these wicked, erroneous doctrines, but should also denounce and refute them with pen and mouth, in order to protect the genuine Dharma of the Buddha.
Paying no heed to the thickness of one's afflictions, no matter the weight of one's karmic hindrances, merely uttering Namo Amitābha Buddha with the mouth, one should think that rebirth is certain.”
No matter the weight of one's offenses, the one who merely recites the Buddha's name gains rebirth.”
Though the power of such evil karma is strong, if one recites the Buddha's name, he does not go against the vow of the compassionate primal vow of Amitābha Buddha, and is certain to be welcomed.”
Recite the name of Amitābha, and at death the Buddha is certain to come to welcome.”
If one commits the five heinous acts
, and comes to hear the six-character name
(comes to hear “Namo Amitābha Buddha”)
, the fiery cart departs of itself
(the fiery cart of hell departs of itself)
, and the lotus dais comes at once to welcome.”

This says: an utterly evil person who has committed the five heinous offenses, so long as he has heard the Buddha-name, and even without reciting it, is reborn in the Western Paradise of Ultimate Bliss to enjoy all bliss forever. If this truly were so, what evil deed in the world would anyone not dare to do? Does this match reality? Is this how the Buddha-Dharma teaches sentient beings?
As for
how one is able to be reborn in the Western Paradise of Ultimate Bliss
, Master Shandao, the manifestation of Amitābha, states it clearly and distinctly
(see in detail the article
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teaching
It is precisely because upholding the Name is easy,
that in continuity one is reborn
. If one can be
thought after thought continuous
even until the end of life
then of ten, ten are reborn; of a hundred, a hundred are reborn.
I pray all people reflect well, and that whether walking, standing, sitting or lying, they must
arouse the mind and restrain
spur and restrain oneself
day and night never ceasing
, so that with the death of the final thought, the next thought is born [in the Pure Land].
Forever enjoying the unconditioned Dharma-bliss, and even attaining Buddhahood — how could this not be a delight!

Master Shandao is the manifestation of Amitābha Buddha; his words are the words of Amitābha Buddha. As to how one can attain rebirth, of course his words are the criterion! Those who recite the Buddha's name must engrave this upon their heart and mind, believing it ever more, relying on it ever more.
This Honen actually says the reverse: What need is there of “in continuity one is reborn”? What need is there of “arouse the mind and restrain the self”? Even if
an utterly evil person who has committed the five heinous offenses
(“if one commits the five heinous acts”)
, so long as he has heard the Buddha-name
(“comes to hear the six-character name”)
, he is at once reborn
(“the fiery cart departs of itself, the lotus dais comes at once to welcome”)
Can this be called
based
on Master Shandao, the manifestation of Amitābha, and his Pure Land thought”? Can this be called “
obtaining
the very marrow of Master Shandao”
And so forth.
From the above we can see that Master Shandao taught
“continued recitation leads to rebirth”
“earnest self-restraint”
, while Master Hōnen, in sharp and pointed contrast, loudly advocated
“reciting the Name surely leads to rebirth
(and even hearing the Name surely leads to rebirth)
and
“the evil person as the principal subject

(advocating that not only is earnest self-restraint unnecessary, but one may freely commit every sort of evil—killing one’s father, killing one’s mother, killing an arhat, shedding the Buddha’s blood, and sowing discord in the Sangha—all of it is permitted! —“The fire cart departs of itself; the lotus dais comes at once to welcome.”)
“Recitation of the Name surely leads to rebirth”
and
“the evil person as the principal subject”
—these two points are the
essential heart
of the Primal Vow Dharma Gate.
It cleverly exploits such human weaknesses as fear of hardship, love of shortcuts, and craving for worldly pleasures in order to deceive its followers.

“Recitation of the Name surely leads to rebirth” is the theoretical basis for monastics having no need to cultivate, while “the evil person as the principal subject” is the theoretical basis for monastics having no need to observe the precepts or to abandon evil and practice good. Accordingly, monastics degenerated from practitioners into professional monks who neither kept the precepts nor cultivated, letting their hair grow, eating meat, taking wives, committing evil—anything at all was permissible. The sad thing is that they still believed they would surely be reborn, confident because these two points, “recitation of the Name surely leads to rebirth” and “the evil person as the principal subject,” guaranteed it—little realizing that this was all a pack of deceptive lies! See
the article “The Primal Vow Dharma Gate Is a Non-Buddhist Adjunct”
and

“Recitation of the Name surely leads to rebirth” and “the evil person as the principal subject”
—these two points are the essential heart of the Primal Vow Dharma Gate] These are Master Hōnen’s very own words. Hōnen said:
The
essential heart
of the Pure Land school lies in this: whoever recites the Buddha’s name, no matter who they are, is reborn.
Even if there be no equal in the world
(nothing comparable)
to such an evil person
, if one recites Namo Amitābha Buddha,
even a single thought suffices for rebirth.
This not only failed to grasp the essential marrow of Master Shandao’s teaching but was a deliberate
falsification of
the Pure Land thought of Master Shandao, the incarnation of Amitābha, in order to establish the Primal Vow Dharma Gate
. For eight hundred years, who knows how many practitioners’ wisdom lives have been ruined by this!
